metadata.title: Amos
metadata.subtitle: Amos 1:1 – 9:15 (27 questions)
metadata.description: Questions on the Book of Amos according to the King James Version (1769).
metadata.author: King James Version (1769)

questions.text: According to Amos 1:1, what was Amos before he prophesied concerning Israel?

options.text: A priest from Beth-el
An herdman of Tekoa
A scribe of the king
A merchant of Samaria

questions.text: For what transgression does the LORD announce judgment upon Damascus in Amos 1:3?

options.text: Because they worshipped idols and laid waste the land of Israel
Because they spoiled Israel and took captive all the border cities
Because they have threshed Gilead with threshing instruments of iron
Because they slew the messengers and violated the solemn covenant

questions.text: What transgression of the children of Ammon is condemned in Amos 1:13?

options.text: They burned the standing corn and carried away the cattle of Israel
They spoiled the holy treasures and plundered the cities of Judah
They enslaved the children of Judah and delivered them up to Edom
They have ripped up the women with child of Gilead, to enlarge their border

questions.text: Why is judgment pronounced upon Moab in Amos 2:1?

options.text: Because he burned the bones of the king of Edom into lime
Because they attacked Israel and destroyed the fruitful land
Because they worshipped false gods and sacrificed their children
Because they sold the captives and broke the covenant of brotherhood

questions.text: What transgression of Israel does the LORD condemn in Amos 2:6?

options.text: They sacrifice upon the high places and bow to heathen idols
They sold the righteous for silver, and the poor for a pair of shoes
They profane the sabbath day and labor on holy feast days
They withhold the holy tithes and neglect the house of the LORD

questions.text: According to Amos 2:12, how did Israel treat the Nazarites and the prophets?

options.text: They drove them into exile and suffered them not to return into the land
They honored them as messengers of God and hearkened to all their words
They gave the Nazarites wine to drink, and commanded the prophets: Prophesy not
They disregarded them and gave no heed to their preaching and prophecy

questions.text: According to Amos 3:2, what consequence follows Israel being known of God?

options.text: God will make them rich and prosper all their works
God will spare them always and pardon all their guilt
God will grant them peace from all their fierce enemies
God will punish them for all their iniquities

questions.text: Why can Amos not keep silent according to Amos 3:8?

options.text: The Lord GOD hath spoken, who can but prophesy?
The people desire it of him and grant him no rest
The king commandeth him and directeth all his speech
He desireth to make himself a great name in the land

questions.text: What judgment upon the buildings does Amos 3:14-15 proclaim?

options.text: The walls of Samaria shall be strengthened, and the palaces shall stand
The altars of Beth-el shall be cut off, and the houses of ivory shall perish
A new sanctuary shall be built, and the throne of the kingdom established
The heathen nations shall make peace, and warfare shall cease from the land

questions.text: How does Amos 4:1 describe the oppressive women in the mountain of Samaria?

options.text: Proud daughters of Zion, walking with wanton eyes and costly ornaments
Well-fed sheep in the fold, trusting in their riches and doing no good
Kine of Bashan, which oppress the poor, which crush the needy, saying: Bring!
Pampered noblewomen of the palace, taking no thought for the afflicted

questions.text: Which refrain is repeated as an indictment in Amos 4:6-11?

options.text: Be strong and of good courage, saith the LORD your God
Yet will I bless you and keep you, saith the LORD unto you
Fear not, neither be dismayed, saith the LORD your God
Yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the LORD

questions.text: What call is given to Israel in Amos 4:12?

options.text: Prepare to meet thy God, O Israel
Flee, O Israel, for the day of wrath is come
Turn again, O Israel, and seek the LORD thy God
Offer sacrifices, O Israel, for thy Maker is holy

questions.text: What does the LORD say unto the house of Israel in Amos 5:4?

options.text: Sacrifice unto me, and ye shall live
Seek ye me, and ye shall live
Fear my name, and ye shall live
Hearken unto me, and ye shall live

questions.text: What will the day of the LORD be to those who desire it (Amos 5:18)?

options.text: Joy and not sorrow unto the soul
Light and not darkness to the people
Darkness, and not light
Peace and not sudden destruction

questions.text: What does Amos 5:24 urge to flow forth?

options.text: Faithfulness as a great rock, and peace like a flowing river
Sacrifice like sweet incense, and thanksgiving like a stream
Praise like the sound of waters, and grace like a holy hill
Judgment like waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream

questions.text: Upon whom does Amos 6:1 pronounce a woe?

options.text: To them that are at ease in Zion, and trust in the mountain of Samaria
Upon the false priests in Beth-el, who seek only their own advantage
Upon the herdmen of Tekoa, who have left their sheep without pasture
Upon the unjust traders at the gate, who use deceitful measures

questions.text: How does Amos 6:4 describe the luxurious living of the wanton?

options.text: They build palaces of cedar wood and deck their courts with fine silver
They lie upon beds of ivory, and eat calves out of the midst of the stall
They clothe themselves in scarlet silk and boast of precious treasures
They drink rich wine continually and make merry in all the open streets

questions.text: What fate is proclaimed in Amos 6:7 for those who stretch themselves upon couches?

options.text: They shall pay tribute and serve the king of Assyria for evermore
They shall abide in their houses and keep their great riches in peace
They shall go captive with the first that go captive into exile
They shall become bondmen and possess no inheritance in the land

questions.text: How did Amos intercede for the people in Amos 7:2?

options.text: O Lord GOD, send forth a deliverer, that Jacob may be saved!
O Lord GOD, smite the adversaries that oppress Jacob so sorely!
O Lord GOD, take my life instead, that thy chosen people may live!
O Lord GOD, forgive, I beseech thee: by whom shall Jacob arise?

questions.text: What did the Lord hold in his hand in Amos 7:7?

options.text: A plumbline, by which the wall was made
A drawn sword, wherewith he smote the enemy
A pair of balances, wherewith he weighed sins
A shepherd staff, wherewith he numbered sheep

questions.text: What did Amos answer unto Amaziah the priest (Amos 7:14)?

options.text: I am a priest of the LORD, serving in the sanctuary at Beth-el from youth
I was no prophet, neither a prophet's son; but a gatherer of sycomore fruit
I am a royal scribe of the king, speaking only by his decree to the nation
I am a holy prophet from Judah, come up of my own accord unto Beth-el

questions.text: What did the basket of summer fruit signify in Amos 8:2?

options.text: A joyful harvest season was about to begin for all Israel
The acceptable day of repentance had come for the nation
The end is come upon my people of Israel
The wrath of the LORD should tarry yet for many years

questions.text: What dishonest practice is condemned in Amos 8:5?

options.text: Taking usury and withholding silver from the fatherless and poor
Stealing the cattle of neighbours and selling them upon the market
Withholding the holy tithes and robbing the ministers of the temple
Making the ephah small, and the shekel great, and falsifying balances

questions.text: What famine is foretold in Amos 8:11?

options.text: Not a famine of bread, but of hearing the words of the LORD
A grievous famine of bread and grain that consumeth the whole land
A sore thirst for pure water that causeth man and beast to perish
A great drought upon the earth that drieth up all fountains of waters

questions.text: What does Amos 9:2 declare concerning the inescapable judgment of God?

options.text: Whosoever fleeth to the sanctuary shall be preserved from destruction
Though they dig into hell, thence shall mine hand take them
Whosoever hideth in the mountains shall be safe from all punishment
Only those remaining in Samaria shall be overtaken by the destroyer

questions.text: What does the LORD promise to raise up in Amos 9:11?

options.text: To build again a glorious temple of hewn stones in Jerusalem
To divide the promised land anew among the twelve tribes of Israel
To raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and build it
To make an everlasting covenant of peace with his chosen people

questions.text: With what promise does Amos 9:14 conclude?

options.text: The destruction of the sanctuary and the carrying away of Israel into exile
The judgment upon all surrounding nations that had afflicted God's heritage
A solemn call to repentance and mourning addressed to the house of Israel
To bring again the captivity of Israel, that they shall build the waste cities
